coach.text: Solid, efficient pick with a strong win-rate profile — good take for pick one [SIG-01]. Since nothing is committed yet, this is fine as a foundation but stay flexible and keep evaluating the next few picks on raw power before locking into green [SIG-02].

Bigfin Bouncer is a fine pick with solid tempo value and good stats, but it wasn't clearly the best card in the pack—Hero's Downfall and High Fae Trickster were passed at much earlier ATAs, meaning others rate them higher, and Hero's Downfall in particular is premium removal that answers anything [EVAL-03]. Still, at pick 2 with no colors committed, taking a strong blue card is perfectly reasonable [SIG-01][SIG-02].

Ruby, Daring Tracker is an efficient two-mana mana-fixer with a real upside clause, and taking the top card in the pack at pick 3 while staying flexible is exactly right [SIG-02]. It also lines up with your green card already in pool, giving you a soft early lean into Red/Green without fully committing [SIG-01].

Eager Trufflesnout is a strong beater — trample plus recurring Food value — and it's on-color with your green base already, so this is a clean, easy correct pick [EVAL-08]. It also fits well against Ruby, Daring Tracker if you lean Gruul aggro-midrange next [ARCH-03].

Involuntary Employment fits neatly with your existing Red/Green cards (Ruby, Daring Tracker) and Red splash (nothing wasted here) — a great tempo/value swing that also fixes mana via the Treasure [EVAL-01][EVAL-04]. You're still only 5 picks in, so leaning Red-Green off a Green base is a reasonable, not premature, commitment [SIG-02].

Solid removal is worth taking even off-color this early — a splash-friendly single-pip kill spell is a fine hedge while your Red/Green base is still thin [SIG-02]. Just note Rugged Highlands was sitting right there for your actual colors, so keep an eye on whether White is really opening up or you'll need to pivot back soon [SIG-07].

Quilled Greatwurm is a huge finisher that snowballs fast in a Red/Green deck already leaning aggressive with Sylvan Scavenging and Daring Tracker — an easy top pick with no real competition in this pack [EVAL-02][SIG-02]. Just keep an eye on your curve since a 6-drop this steep needs enough early plays to survive to cast it [CURVE-03][MISTAKE-06].

Felidar Savior is a strong lifelink+counters payoff, and taking it as a light White splash off Red/Green makes sense given it's the raw best card in the pack [EVAL-02]. With two White cards already (Luminous Rebuke, Felidar Savior) it's worth keeping the splash lane open, but don't over-commit until you see if White fixing actually shows up [MISTAKE-03].

Bloodfell Caves is off-color for a White/Red/Green deck (Rakdos fixing), so it's not actually feeding your mana base at all — you're three colors deep in your actual pool and this card supports neither of the two you'd splash into [MANA-01]. Wildwood Scourge is a fine on-color green two-drop with scaling upside that fits your existing curve and colors far better [CURVE-01]; taking a dual land for colors you're not in is a wasted pick this late into color commitment [MISTAKE-03].

Solid, uncontested pick — Apothecary Stomper is a big vigilance body with a flexible upside mode, and it slots right into your Green base [EVAL-08]. Just note your curve is getting top-heavy with Quilled Greatwurm and this six-drop both in the mix, so prioritize cheaper plays soon to keep the deck from stalling early [CURVE-03].

Mischievous Mystic is a strong two-drop flier with real upside, but it's off your committed White/Red/Green colors and pulls you into a fourth color you've barely touched [SIG-07][MISTAKE-03]. If you're not actually pivoting to blue, Dwynen, Gilt-Leaf Daen would have stayed on-plan for your green base while still being a solid body [EVAL-10]. Fine pick if you're genuinely open to reshaping colors this early in pack 2, but be honest that this is a real color commitment, not a freebie [SIG-11].

Ashroot Animist is a strong 4/4 trample that pumps a teammate on attack, and it slots right into your Red/Green core alongside Ruby, Daring Tracker [EVAL-08]. With four colors still active this late, this pick also reinforces you should be narrowing toward Red/Green as your primary pair rather than staying spread thin [SIG-11].

Correct pick — a mana-ramping, land-fixing, self-mill payoff engine fits your green-heavy pool perfectly and grades out as the pack's best card [EVAL-02][SIG-02]. With four colors floating, the extra land drop and eventual card advantage also help stabilize your mana base [MANA-03]; just keep pushing to actually settle into two (or a clear main-plus-splash) soon [MISTAKE-03].

Scrawling Crawler is a colorless 3/2 that slots into any of your four colors with a strong card-advantage upkeep trigger, and the data confirms it's both the raw best and best-for-deck pick here [EVAL-08]. Good value grab given you're still juggling four colors — colorless power is exactly what keeps your options flexible right now [SIG-01].

Dismal Backwater is off your actual colors (you're WURG-leaning, not blue/black), so despite the A+ grade this pick is really just a fine fixing land you likely won't play — the "best card" is only best in a vacuum here [MISTAKE-03]. With four colors already touched, you should be prioritizing fixing that supports your real pairs or a strong on-color playable like Balmor if you're in red/blue, not a U/B dual [SIG-11].

You already own zero black cards besides this one, and it's the only thing pulling you toward a fifth color when White/Blue/Red/Green are established — that's a real cost even though it graded as the best raw card in the pack [MISTAKE-03]. Gnarlid Colony was right there, on-color for Green, cheap, high-maindeck rate, and fits your curve far better [CURVE-01]; taking the off-color bomb this late in your color commitment risks a card that never makes the deck [SIG-12].

You're clearly four-color at this point, so any fixing is gold; Evolving Wilds smooths all your splashes without committing you further [MANA-03]. Given your pool's messy color spread, prioritize more fixing and signpost cards like this over the black cards, which don't fit your committed colors [MISTAKE-03].

Solid pick — you're four colors deep already and a big card-draw spell like this smooths out mana issues while refilling your hand late [EVAL-07]. That said, with WUBRG this scattered, remember you still need to commit to two real colors soon and shore up your curve rather than keep collecting the best card in a vacuum [MISTAKE-03] [SIG-11].

Tranquil Cove is exactly the fixing your four-color soup needs given you're spread across White/Blue/Red/Green — it directly supports your White/Blue cards while gaining a bit of life [MANA-01]. With this many colors committed, prioritizing fixing over marginal playables is correct, though you should still aim to narrow to two or three colors by the back half of pack 2 [SIG-11].

You're four colors deep with a messy pool — Scoured Barrens fixes for white/black, but you have zero real black cards and this doesn't even help your green/blue/red core stabilize [MANA-03]. Taking fixing is reasonable at this point in the draft, but you badly need to cut down to two colors soon; this pick just delays that reckoning rather than solving it [MISTAKE-03].

Correct pick by a wide margin — flash flying 3/3 with recurring value is a bomb-tier common/uncommon and slots straight into your blue base [EVAL-02]. You're four colors deep though, so it's time to cut a color rather than keep spreading; blue and green look like your core with red/green support cards already in hand [MISTAKE-03].

Cheap efficient removal that scales down to a real threat, and a second copy stacks nicely with your existing Luminous Rebuke [EVAL-03]. You're already four colors deep, which is risky, but this pick is unambiguously correct on power and fits the white removal shell you're building [MISTAKE-03].

Solid pick — a second Felidar Savior gives you another lifelink body with a built-in counters payoff, which fits neatly with your green +1/+1 counter theme (Ashroot Animist, Quilled Greatwurm) [EVAL-08]. With four colors still in the pool, you should be prioritizing consolidating into your best two, and a repeatable white creature that reinforces your existing plan is exactly the kind of pick that helps you commit [SIG-11].

Stab is efficient removal, but you're already four colors deep with zero committed black cards besides one Soul-Shackled Zombie — this is speculative at pick 32 of 42, with only 10 picks left to actually build a black base [MISTAKE-03]. With this pool that thin on focus, Overrun would've at least reinforced your actual Green commitment; taking a stray black card this late risks it never making the deck [DECK-05].

Strongbox Raider is a strong aggressive body with card advantage upside, and it's the correct raw and contextual pick given your Red splash-turned-real-color already has Involuntary Employment and the R/G cards [EVAL-01][EVAL-02]. That said, you're now sprawling across five colors on 33 cards — with only two mono-Red cards so far, make sure Red is actually earning its slot rather than just accumulating strong loose cards [MISTAKE-03].

You're five colors deep with no real plan yet — that's a problem in itself, but this pick is fine on its face: Cathar Commando is a flash 3/1 that ambushes attackers and doubles as artifact/enchantment removal, a flexible efficient body regardless of your final colors [EVAL-01][EVAL-04]. With 8 picks left you need to actually cut down to two colors soon; White/Green or White/Blue look like your deepest lanes right now, so start prioritizing fixing and cards in those pairs over spreading further [MISTAKE-03].

Solid conditional removal that only costs one white pip, so it's easy to fit whichever two colors you settle into [MANA-07]. At pick 35 you're this deep with five colors barely committed anywhere — you badly need to lock into two colors now and prioritize creatures/curve over more removal [SIG-11][MISTAKE-03], but as a pure card-quality pick this was correct [EVAL-03].

Tolarian Terror slots straight into your blue instant/sorcery shell as a cheap-cast, evasive-ward 5/5 finisher, and it's clearly both the raw and context best card here [EVAL-02]. This late in the draft with only 6 picks left, locking in a bomb-quality closer for your best-supported color pair is exactly right [SIG-11].

Fine pick this late — you're clearly five-color soup right now, so any fixing land helps, and Scoured Barrens directly supports your White/Black cards like Felidar Savior and Stab [MANA-01]. With only 5 picks left, you should be narrowing to two colors soon rather than continuing to hoover up fixing for a pile of splashes [MISTAKE-03].

This late in the draft you're still five colors deep with only a handful of playables per color — the fixing land is exactly what you need to actually cast a deck, especially given White/Blue looks like your strongest pair right now [MANA-01]. Good, low-risk pick with 4 to go; keep prioritizing fixing and playables over marginal power at this stage [MISTAKE-03].
